comparisons.corpus_what: calendar 2025 capex of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft (cash purchases of property and equipment, Meta's own total)
comparisons.explanation: Three outlets give the same $410B for the same four companies. The corpus's cash figure is $378.6B; adding the finance-lease additions the filings state for Amazon ($2.9B), Alphabet ($1.6B) and Microsoft ($25.2B for the calendar year, built from its fiscal-year filings) gives $408.3B, within $1.7B (0.4%). The gap is the lease treatment: the outlets' figure includes finance leases.

comparisons.corpus_what: calendar 2026 to 2026-09-30, capex of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and SpaceX: the sum of the five company-year estimates (cash purchases of property and equipment, except Meta's own total)
comparisons.explanation: Same five companies and the same period. The outlet's figure sits between the corpus's cash-only sum ($547.6B) and that sum plus the finance-lease additions the filings state for Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft ($569.0B to $571.9B; Meta's figure already includes finance-lease principal), so the gap is a matter of which lease amounts the outlet counted. The outlet's page lists no per-company figures, so the split cannot be checked.

comparisons.corpus_what: latest full-year guidance of Amazon (about $220B, cash capex), Alphabet ($195B to $205B, midpoint), Meta ($135B to $145B, midpoint) and Microsoft (about $170B for the calendar year), $730B, plus SpaceX's nine-month actual of $48.1B (the graph holds no SpaceX full-year guidance)
comparisons.explanation: The corpus total has no SpaceX fourth-quarter figure. SpaceX's third quarter alone was $19.6B (nine months $48.069B less six months $28.476B, derived); adding one such quarter gives about $797.7B, within $5.3B of the outlet's low end. The remainder lies in the choice of point within each company's guidance range and in the Microsoft lease treatment.

comparisons.corpus_what: latest full-year guidance midpoints of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft (range $720B to $740B)
comparisons.explanation: Same four companies, a forward figure for 2026. The outlet's figure is $10B above the top of the corpus's guidance range and was reported on 12 October, before the third-quarter calls that set the corpus's latest guidance; the outlet shows no per-company figures. The date of the original Businessweek article was read second-hand.

comparisons.corpus_what: latest full-year guidance midpoints of the same four companies
comparisons.explanation: Same four companies. The outlet's 30 April figure is $5B below the corpus's October midpoint total; between April and October Alphabet's guidance rose from $175B-$185B to $195B-$205B and Meta's from $125B-$145B to $135B-$145B, which more than accounts for the difference. The outlet's page was read through a repost.

comparisons.corpus_what: latest guidance midpoints of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft ($730B) plus Oracle's nine months of calendar 2026 to date ($63.6B; Oracle's fiscal-2027 capex guidance covers June 2026 to May 2027 and is not a calendar figure)
comparisons.explanation: The outlet's five companies are the four plus Oracle. The corpus has no calendar-2026 forecast for Oracle (only nine months of actuals and a fiscal-year range), so its Oracle share is a partial-year actual; Oracle's last quarter of the calendar year is the main missing piece. The outlet's estimate dates from May.

comparisons.corpus_what: equity inflow claims starting in the first quarter of 2026 (the 42 equity claims starting in 2026 total $300.5B; the quarter's $132.7B is computed from the claims' start dates)
comparisons.explanation: The corpus counts the rounds it holds (frontier labs and infrastructure builders) and public offerings, with the large rounds that dominate the outlet's quarter (OpenAI's $122B round closed March 2026); the outlet counts every venture round worldwide in AI. The corpus has no claim for the long tail of rounds, so it sits below the outlet; the split between the missing rounds and any scope difference needs the outlet's deal list, which its page does not give.
comparisons.outlet_text: AI shattered records last quarter, with $242 billion

comparisons.corpus_what: debt inflow claims starting in 2026, all borrowers, to date

comparisons.explanation: The Census Bureau's construction-spending series counts the value of data-center buildings put in place in the United States (calendar 2025: about $49.7B, summed from its monthly not-seasonally-adjusted file by the research agent).
